purpose: Where to look for a scientific illustration, and what has to be true before one enters a lesson. This lists candidate pools and the licence rule they have to satisfy. It does not certify any individual file: licences on these sites are set per item and change, so the author verifies the specific file, records the evidence in lesson.json thirdPartyAssets, and appends what they found to site/agent/source-access-ledger.json.

acceptedLicences.note: Set by lesson.schema.json. Share-alike licences are absent deliberately and are not a gap to fill casually: CC BY-SA obliges an adaptation to carry the same licence, and cropping, relabelling, or recolouring a figure makes an adaptation. Most illustrations on general encyclopaedic media sites are BY-SA, so that pool is mostly unusable here. Prefer public-domain government galleries and CC BY 4.0 medical-art libraries, where the whole collection is one licence and the check is quick.

candidatePools.name: NIH NIGMS Image and Video Gallery
candidatePools.expect: Cell structure, organelles, microscopy, molecular machinery.
candidatePools.why: A US government gallery, so many items are public domain, but it also hosts contributed images under other terms. The item page states the terms for that item.

candidatePools.name: NCI Visuals Online
candidatePools.expect: Cells, tissue, and process illustrations produced for the National Cancer Institute.
candidatePools.why: Many items are US government work in the public domain; some are credited to outside illustrators with their own terms.

candidatePools.name: Servier Medical Art
candidatePools.expect: A large library of medical and cell-biology drawing components.
candidatePools.why: Published under a Creative Commons licence, but the version has changed over time and only CC BY 4.0 is accepted here. Confirm the version shown on the site at the time of use.

candidatePools.name: EMBL-EBI training materials
candidatePools.why: Training material is frequently CC BY, stated per page.

candidatePools.name: Wikimedia Commons
candidatePools.why: Licences are per file and a large share are CC BY-SA, which this project does not accept. Usable only where a specific file is CC0, public domain, or CC BY 4.0, and the file page is the evidence.

candidatePools.name: BioRender
candidatePools.why: Figures are licensed to the subscriber who makes them, under terms that do not permit redistribution under this project's content licence.

candidatePools.name: Textbook and publisher figures
candidatePools.why: Redrawing one does not remove the original expression. The rights policy names a lightly redrawn figure as still carrying it. Build the figure from the underlying anatomy instead.

beforeUse: Confirm the licence on the item's own page, not on the site's front page or a search result.
Record source URL, title, creator, licence, and the evidence you read in lesson.json thirdPartyAssets.
State whether you modified it, and how, in the same record. Cropping, relabelling, and recolouring are modifications.
Give the file a pack-local copy under assets/; never hotlink.
Append the domain and what you found to site/agent/source-access-ledger.json.
qualityBar: The structure shown is correct and current, and the lesson can state what it is looking at without hedging.
Labels are legible at the size a learner reads, and in English, or absent so the lesson can caption them.
Meaning survives without colour: a reader who cannot separate red from green still gets the point.
The alt text and long description can carry the whole teaching point, because some readers will only get those.
No watermark, no house branding, no embedded citation to a third party's own figure.
It teaches the thing the scene needs, rather than being decoration that happens to be biological.
